html:
The Ottoman conquest of Bosnia took place mainly in 1463, when Sultan Mehmed II overran the kingdom in a few weeks and had its last king, Stephen Tomašević, executed at Jajce.

Bosnia had been weakened by quarrels among its nobles and by its refusal to pay tribute. Hungary briefly retook Jajce and held it until 1527, and Herzegovina fell in stages by 1482. The Ottomans made Bosnia a province on their frontier with Hungary and Venice. Over the next century much of the population, including many nobles, converted to Islam, while Catholics and Orthodox Christians stayed as protected subjects. Ottoman rule lasted until the Austro Hungarian occupation of 1878.
